pattern_stance_changes.reason: The router clearly beats random routing at the same budget (Table 2: 37 vs 14.4 expected repairs). Against the realistic status quo, route-all, it trades away 35 of 72 repairs (recall 0.514) for 80% fewer calls. In the only measured LLM pilot (Table 3), the router keeps 4 of 5 true-positive escalations, n=5. The 'expensive path' is a single DeepSeek diagnosis prompt, not a repair agent, so the paper shows a budget–recall trade-off on historical labels rather than a routing win on agent outcomes.

The 'budget' is the top-k% routing threshold, i.e. the same evidence already counted under P23. The pilot's 66.7% call and 66.1% token reductions follow from evaluating 20 of 60 PRs, one call each (§4.3). No cap or budget on agent spend is tested against an uncapped alternative.

missed_issues: Noise floor: the richer initial-PR T0 regime, which has strictly more information than creation-time, scores lower (top-20% recall 0.472 vs 0.514, 34 vs 37 repairs; Tables 1–2). Differences of a few positives are within noise at n=72, yet no fold variance or CIs are reported. The creation-time result was also picked from an exploratory model search without nested selection (§5).

The labels may be coupled to the features. One annotator labeled each PR while reading its record, including the title and commits (§4.1). The creation-time router then predicts those labels from the title, so annotator cues and title wording are not independent.

Transfer to production streams is overstated by the enriched pool. Candidates were retrieved with repair-like search terms ('fix, test, build, pin, rollback, API'; §4.1). In a natural Dependabot/Renovate stream, the base rate and therefore precision@20% would be lower and calls per repair higher than 2.68.

The pilot's four arms are disjoint PR pools (top, random, bottom; §4.3). 'All-agent' is the union of the three samples, not a matched run of the same PRs, and TP counts of 5, 4, 1 and 0 cannot support a retention rate.

A strong, cheap, deterministic alternative is never compared: escalating only PRs whose own CI build or tests fail on the update. The review's applicability raises it, but its absence also weakens the routing claim itself.
note: I agree with admit_with_caveats as a preliminary short paper with a sound hindsight-leakage protocol. The routing (P23) supports stance overstates a budget–recall trade-off measured on historical labels and a 60-PR, single-prompt pilot. The cost-budget (P24) stance double-counts the same routing knob.
